name: Nature and sustainability
purpose: environment, carbon and energy, sustainable sourcing and supply chains in the real world, water and pollution, land use and biodiversity, outdoor safety

scenes.what: the solar farm on the flat valley floor seen from its gravel maintenance track: a wildflower meadow, then long rows of south-facing panels with sheep grazing between them, and the wind turbines on the ridge beyond
scenes.for: renewable energy and where electricity comes from, why output varies with sun and wind, Scope 2 emissions and green power contracts, land sharing and biodiversity, a site visit to a supplier or an energy project
plan: Metres: x to the right (east), y away from the camera (north), z up. The ground is flat at z 0 here.

The camera stands at the south edge of the solar farm, inside its deer fence, on a grassy verge beside the gravel maintenance track that runs east to west across the view from y 5 to y 8.5 (about 3.5 m wide).
North of the track, a wildflower meadow left unplanted as a pollinator strip fills y 8.5 to 50.

The panel rows run east to west across the whole view, the first with its front (lower, south) edge at y 50, then every 9 m (y 59, 68, 77 and on to about y 300). Each row is a table of panels about 4.2 m deep on the ground, 0.8 m high at its front edge and 2.75 m high at its back edge, tilted about 25 degrees to face south toward the camera, on galvanised steel posts. Grass between the rows; sheep graze there, about (6, 63) and (-14, 72). A small green inverter cabin (6 by 2.5 m, 2.9 m tall) stands in a gap between rows at x -41 to -35, y 92; a weather station mast 3 m tall at the right end of the front row (10.9, 51.5).

Beyond the solar farm the valley floor runs north about 1.5 km to the foot of the ridge, which rises to a crest about 60 m above the valley, 2 km away. Wind turbines on the crest: one at (-560, 2000), one at (250, 2000), a third further left at (-1250, 2000), each 100 m to the hub with a 130 m rotor.
Cast: A and B stand on the gravel track, A at about (-0.6, 6.0) and B at about (0.2, 6.3), side by side, looking out over the panels.
Camera: x 0, y 0, eye 1.3 m (so standing heads rise above the ridge into the sky), turned 8 degrees left of due north; 50 mm lens (about 45 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 50 percent.
The head rays pass about 1 m over the front row's back edge and are still rising when they reach the ridge (about 90 m up there, above its 60 m crest): both heads are seen against open sky.
scenes.camera: A low standing camera on the verge of the solar farm's maintenance track, eye 1.3 m, turned 8 degrees left of due north toward the ridge; 50 mm lens, about 45 degrees across; no tilt. Horizon at y 540 (50 percent). Lines running away from the camera (the track's edges seen end on, the posts' lines between rows) meet at x 1286 on the horizon; the rows and the track run across the frame almost level (their vanishing point is far off-frame left), rising very slightly toward the left.
scenes.composition: The sky fills the top half. The ridge's crest crosses the frame as a soft, slightly rising line at about y 485 at the left edge, y 471 at the centre and y 466 at the right; its lower slopes of small hedged fields fall to the horizon band. On the crest, the two turbines in view: one at x 649 (tower from y 474 up to the hub at y 361, rotor about 145 px across, blade tips reaching y 288 and y 435), one at x 1586 (tower from y 470 to the hub at y 351, tips at y 274 and y 428); a third stands in the left overscan (x about -72). The solar farm is a long dark-blue band across the middle: the front row's back edge at about y 477 and its front edge at y 563 at the centre, the rows behind it stacking up and thinning toward the horizon (the row at 160 m spans y 520 to 547); the inverter cabin sits among them at the left (x 295 to 432, y 502 to 571), the weather mast at the right end of the front row (x 1800, y 601 up to 460); two sheep in the grass between the first rows (x 838, y 559 and x 1514, y 563). Below the rows, the wildflower meadow fills the frame down to the track, whose far edge crosses at about y 898 and whose gravel runs out of the bottom edge. Focal point: the turbine at x 1586 over the panels, with the cast between the two turbines. Free zones for the cast, both heads in open sky above the ridge, the panel band below the chins: (1) A on the track left of centre, seen full length (head top x 1052, y 366; feet x 1052, y 1043); (2) B on the track right of centre (head top x 1361, y 372; feet x 1361, y 1026). Each head is at least 140 px clear of a turbine's rotor.
scenes.light: Main set: an early-June afternoon, the sun about 50 degrees high in the south-west, behind the camera's left shoulder. The panel faces look south toward the camera: lit, deep blue with a lighter band of reflected sky along their upper halves and thin bright edges on their silver frames; under each row a dark band of shade on the grass, and the shadows of the rows fall away from the camera and to the right. The turbine towers are lit on their left (south-west) sides and pale grey on the right; the rotors stand still or turning slowly (draw the blades crisp). The meadow's flowers and grasses are bright in the sun. A few fair-weather cumulus clouds float over the ridge, their shadows lying as soft darker patches on the ridge's slopes. Far haze: the ridge and turbines a little paler and bluer than the panels.
scenes.far: The sky with its clouds, the ridge with its fields and the three turbines, the valley floor between, all the panel rows with their posts and the grass and shade between them, the sheep, the inverter cabin, the weather mast, and the meadow drawn complete down to the track.
scenes.mid: The gravel track across the lower frame, drawn complete under where the cast stands.
scenes.near: Only a few tall meadow grasses and ox-eye daisies at the lower left corner, cropped by the frame (about x 0 to 240, below y 900); they touch no cast zone.
scenes.motifs_here: the white turbines on the northern ridge, grazing sheep, hedgerows (small on the ridge's slopes)
details: a sheep lying in the shade under the front row of panels
the small dome and white disc of the weather station's sensors on top of its mast
cable trays running along the back of the rows, low to the ground
a strip of red clover and knapweed in the meadow with a few bees

a skylark rising over the meadow
scenes.keep_first: If space is short, keep the sheep in the shade, the weather station, the clover strip and the tyre tracks; drop the rest of the small things before adding anything else.

scenes.what: the edge of a wheat field on a mixed farm on the valley floor, seen from the grass headland inside the field: the crop running away to a far hedgerow with tall oaks, the farmyard's barn and stone farmhouse beyond the right-hand hedge, and the turbine ridge on the skyline
scenes.for: sustainable sourcing and farm visits, Scope 3 emissions in the food chain, soil health and fertiliser use, biodiversity on farmland (hedges and margins), the supply chain's first link
plan: Metres: x to the right (east), y away from the camera (north), z up. The ground is flat at z 0.

The field: winter wheat in early June, about 0.85 m tall and still green with the ears just out, from y 7.5 to the far hedge at y 250, and from far off-frame left to the east hedge at x 60. A grass headland 7.5 m wide runs along the field's south side (y 0 to 7.5), between the crop and the south hedge behind the camera. Tramlines (the paired wheel tracks of the sprayer) run north through the crop every 24 m (x -24, 0, 24, 48).

The far hedgerow (y 250) is hawthorn about 2.5 m tall, with three oaks standing out of it about 20 m tall at x -44, 100 and 186 (the field's north-east corner is at x 60; the hedge carries on east past it). The east hedge (x 60, the same build) separates the field from the farmyard.

The farmyard beyond the east hedge: a steel portal-frame barn 30 m long and 18 m wide, its long open side facing the field, eaves 6 m, ridge 9 m (its west wall line at x 75, from y 135 to 165); a stack of round bales against its south end (66, 128); a two-storey grey stone farmhouse with a slate roof further right (x 119 to 131, y 165 to 177, ridge 8.5 m).

Beyond the farm the valley floor runs north to the ridge, 2.6 km away and about 60 m high, with four wind turbines along its crest about 650 m apart (x -315, 335, 985, 1635 at y 2600), each 100 m to the hub with a 130 m rotor. Left, toward the west, the ridge rises into darker hills with blocks of spruce plantation.
Cast: A stands on the headland at (0.0, 5.6), B a little further along it at (1.6, 6.3), about 1 m in front of the crop's edge, looking at the field.

Camera: x 0, y 0 on the headland, eye 1.3 m (so standing heads rise above the hedges and the ridge into the sky), turned 12 degrees right of due north; 35 mm lens (about 55 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 52 percent.
scenes.camera: A low standing camera on the grass headland, eye 1.3 m, turned 12 degrees right of due north; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt. Horizon at y 562 (52 percent). The tramlines and the field's edges run away to a vanishing point at x 568 on the horizon; the crop's near edge, the far hedge and the ridge run across the frame almost level.
scenes.composition: The sky fills the top half. The ridge crosses the frame at about y 519, rising at the far left into darker spruce-covered hills; on it the four turbines, small and evenly spaced: x 328 (hub y 443), x 810 (hub y 450), x 1244 (hub y 455), x 1637 (hub y 460), each rotor about 95 px across. The far hedgerow is a dark line at y 553 with its three oaks standing above it: x 219 (crown x 152 to 284, top y 416), x 1273 (crown x 1221 to 1325, top y 433) and x 1798 (top y 441). The east hedge enters the right edge at about y 540 and runs left to the field's far corner at x 1008, y 553; beyond it the farmyard: the barn's long open side from x 1367 to 1627 (eaves y 513 to 503, ridge y 482 to 467, base y 575), the bales at its near end (x 1464, top y 547), the farmhouse further right (x 1752 to 1826, ridge y 491 to 495, eaves y 520). The wheat fills the middle: its top surface recedes from the crop's near edge (top edge at about y 675 on the left to y 654 on the right; its foot at about y 888 on the left to y 828 on the right) to the far hedge; the tramlines run from the near edge toward x 568 on the horizon (the one at x 0 runs from x 568, y 868 straight up to y 572). The grass headland fills the bottom of the frame. Focal point: the field running away to the oaks and the turbines. Free zones for the cast, both heads in open sky above the ridge, the turbines and oaks to either side: (1) A on the headland left of centre, seen full length (head top x 565, y 411; feet x 565, y 998), between the turbines at x 328 and x 810; (2) B on the headland right of centre, seen full length (head top x 1035, y 434; feet x 1035, y 931), between the turbine at x 810 and the oak at x 1273.
scenes.light: Main set: an early-June afternoon, the sun about 50 degrees high in the south-west, behind the camera's left shoulder. The wheat is lit bright green with a silvery sheen where the wind bends it; the tramlines read as darker lines. The far hedge and the oaks are lit on their left sides with deep shade inside the crowns; the oaks' shadows fall away and to the right, behind the hedge. The barn's open west side is in light with its inside in deep shadow; the farmhouse's west gable lit. The turbines are white-grey, lit on their left. Fair-weather cumulus over the ridge with soft cloud shadows on its slopes. Far haze: the ridge and the turbines paler and bluer than the hedges.
scenes.far: The sky with its clouds, the ridge with its turbines and the spruce hills at the left, the far hedge with its oaks, the east hedge, the farmyard (barn, bales, farmhouse), the whole wheat field with its tramlines, and the headland drawn complete under where the cast stands.
scenes.mid: A soil auger and a bucket lying on the headland right of B (about x 1250 to 1400, y 900 to 960), and a few wildflowers along the crop's edge.
scenes.near: Only a few tall grass stems at the lower left corner, cropped by the frame (about x 0 to 200, below y 920); they touch no cast zone.
scenes.motifs_here: the white turbines on the northern ridge, a hawthorn hedgerow with tall oaks standing out of it, dark spruce plantations on the western hills
details: a soil auger with a core of dark earth on its blade, and a bucket of soil samples
red poppies along the crop's edge on the headland side
a hare sitting up in a tramline

a pair of buzzards circling over the far hedge
a darker, greener patch of crop where too much fertiliser was spread
scenes.keep_first: If space is short, keep the soil auger and bucket, the poppies, the hare and the bales; drop the rest of the small things before adding anything else.

scenes.what: the river downstream of the valley's food factory, seen from the grassy top of its flood embankment: the water running away upstream between alder-lined banks, a gauge board in the shallows, an outfall headwall in the far bank, and the factory's silos and the turbine ridge in the distance
scenes.for: water pollution and environmental compliance, a spill or discharge incident and how it is reported, water stewardship, flood risk to sites and communities, what happens downstream of a business
plan: Metres: x to the right (east), y away from the camera (north, upstream), z up from the floodplain's grass (z 0). The river's normal water level is z -1.0.

The river: about 25 m wide, from its near (east) bank at x -5 (bank top z 0.5) to its far (west) bank at x -30, running straight north for 600 m toward the factory. Shallow at the edges, gravel showing under clear brown-green water near the banks.

The flood embankment: a grassed earth bank set back from the river, its foot at x -2, its flat crest 3 m wide from x 6.5 to 9.5 at z 2.5, a mown path along the crest. A narrow strip of floodplain grass lies between its foot and the river bank.
On the near bank: a steel staff gauge board fixed to a post in the shallows at (-5.6, 19), from z 1.0 down into the water; a life ring in a red box on a post at (-3.0, 22), 1.7 m tall.

On the far bank: a line of alder trees 12 to 13 m tall (at about y 60, 140 and 230), and a concrete outfall headwall at (-30.5, 85) with a pipe end just above the water (the end of the factory's treated-water pipe, which runs underground along the far bank from the plant). Another alder on the near bank at (-2, 260).

The factory, about 600 m upstream on the far side of the river: four stainless steel silos about 21 m tall at x -140 to -122, and long pale-grey steel sheds about 9 m tall from x -230 to -150. Beyond it the valley floor runs north to the turbine ridge 2.8 km away (about 60 m high) with turbines at x -1870, -1026 and -40.
Cast: A stands on the embankment crest at (7.2, 6.2), looking up the river; B stands on the near bank at the water's edge at (-4.3, 13), a few metres short of the gauge board, with a sample bottle.

Camera: x 8, y 0 on the crest path, eye 1.3 m above the crest (3.8 m above the floodplain), turned 24 degrees left of due north toward the river; 35 mm lens (about 55 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 50 percent.
scenes.camera: A low standing camera on the flood embankment's crest path, eye 1.3 m above the crest, turned 24 degrees left of due north toward the river; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt. Horizon at y 540 (50 percent). The river, its banks and the embankment run away to a vanishing point at x 1781 on the horizon; lines across them run to a point far off-frame left (x about -3180).
scenes.composition: The river is the leading shape: a wedge of water entering from the lower left (the near water's edge at about x 361, y 1001; the near bank's top at x 399, y 860) and narrowing as it runs away to the right toward x 1730 on the horizon; its far bank crosses from off-frame left (x 292, y 657 at 40 m) through x 1055, y 597 to x 1463, y 565. The far bank's alders: a big one at the left (x 602, from the bank at y 625 to its top at y 330), smaller ones at x 1209 (top y 423) and x 1392 (top y 474); a near-bank alder far up at x 1698 (top y 477). The outfall headwall sits in the far bank at x 948 (y 599 to 627). The gauge board stands in the shallows at x 582 (from y 766 down to y 975, in the water); the life ring post on the near bank at x 877 (y 698 to 788). The embankment rises along the right: its crest's river-side edge runs from x 1196, y 1003 up to x 1570, y 707 and on to x 1700, y 605; the mown crest path fills the lower right. In the distance: the factory's silos at x 1290 to 1344 (tops y 488, feet y 552) and its sheds from x 1057 to 1283 (roofs y 525); the ridge at about y 500 to 511 with three turbines at x 640 (hub y 453), x 1080 (hub y 443) and x 1743 (hub y 428), each rotor about 90 px across. Focal point: the river leading up to the factory. Free zones for the cast: (1) A on the crest right of centre, seen full length (head top x 1499, y 402; feet x 1499, y 939), the head in open sky, about 120 px right of the silos and 150 px left of the turbine at x 1743; (2) B on the near bank at the water's edge at the left (head top x 310, y 709; feet x 310, y 901), the head seen against the river's water, about 270 px left of the gauge board.
scenes.light: Main set: an early-June afternoon, the sun about 50 degrees high in the south-west, behind the camera and to its left. The water is brown-green and clear near the near bank (gravel showing), darker in mid-channel, with a band of bright sky reflection and small sun glints toward the right. The alders are lit on their left (south-west) sides with deep shade inside; their reflections lie as darker shapes on the water below them. The embankment's west face (toward the river) is lit; the crest path bright. The factory's silos gleam on their left edges. A few fair-weather clouds; cloud shadows on the ridge. Far haze: the factory and the ridge paler and bluer.
scenes.far: The sky with its clouds, the ridge with its turbines, the factory, the far bank with its alders and the outfall headwall, the river drawn complete to the near bank, the near-bank alder, the gauge board, the life ring post, the floodplain strip, and the embankment with its crest path drawn complete under where A stands.
scenes.mid: Nothing between the camera and the cast: the river bank at B's feet is part of the far layer.
scenes.near: Only a few tall grass stems and a dock leaf on the crest at the lower right corner, cropped by the frame (about x 1700 to 1920, below y 950); they touch no cast zone.
scenes.motifs_here: the white turbines on the northern ridge, the river with alder along its banks, the factory's stainless silos in the distance

scenes.what: a gravel forest road on the valley's western hills where it runs between standing spruce plantation on its left and a felled and newly replanted slope on its right, with stacked timber at the roadside and the valley opening out below to the right
scenes.for: where timber and paper come from, deforestation-free and certified sourcing, carbon stored in forests and replanting after felling, biodiversity in working forests, lone working and outdoor safety
plan: Metres: x to the right (east, downhill), y away from the camera (north, along the road), z up from the road's surface (z 0). The camera is about 150 m above the valley floor.

The road: a gravel forest road with a 3.4 m running width (x -1.7 to 1.7) cut level along the hillside, running straight north for about 220 m and then into the trees. On its right, a gravel turning and loading bay about 4 m wide (x 1.7 to 6) along the first 15 m.

Left of the road (uphill, rising about 30 percent): standing Sitka spruce plantation, 27 m tall, its edge 4.5 m from the road's centre behind a grass verge and a drainage ditch. Timber is stacked on the left verge from y 14 to 26: logs about 4 m long, piled about 3 m high, cut ends toward the road.

Right of the road (downhill, falling about 20 percent): a coupe felled two years ago and replanted, from the road's edge to y 220: low stumps, brash (cut branches) in rows, young spruce about 0.5 m tall planted in lines between them, and a few young broadleaves in pale tree shelters. A small group of birch trees about 14 m tall was left standing at about (9, 70).

The coupe's far edge (y 220) is standing spruce again from the road to x 100; beyond x 100 the slope drops away open, so the valley shows: hedged fields and the river far below, and across the valley the ridge (about 60 m above the valley floor, 3 km away) with its turbines, one of them in view at about (2416, 3000).
Cast: A and B stand on the loading bay at the coupe's edge, A at about (3.2, 5.9), B at about (4.7, 6.6), looking out over the replanted slope.
Camera: x 0, y 0 on the road, eye 1.5 m, turned 14 degrees right of due north; 35 mm lens (about 55 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 50 percent.
scenes.camera: A standing camera on the forest road, eye 1.5 m, turned 14 degrees right of due north; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt. Horizon at y 540 (50 percent). The road and the forest edge on the left run to a vanishing point at x 500 on the horizon, where the road enters the trees; lines across the road run to a point far off-frame right.
scenes.composition: The standing spruce makes a tall dark wall down the left side: it runs out of the top of the frame near the camera and steps down along the road, its tops at y 41 at 100 m (x 411) and y 309 at 215 m (x 459), its foot from x 273, y 591 to x 459, y 549. The timber stack sits on the left verge in front of it (x 88 to 283, top from y 326 near to y 427 far, foot about y 754), cut ends toward us. The road runs from the bottom (left edge x 152, right edge x 820 at y about 830) to the dark gap where it enters the trees ahead (x 485 to 515 at y 553, the gap's top at y 320). The coupe's far edge of spruce crosses from the road (x 527, top y 320) down to the right, its tops at y 353 (x 674) and y 426 (x 1000), ending at x 1300 (top y 493, foot y 702). The felled, replanted slope fills the middle and lower right, falling away to the right; the birch group stands in it at x 744 (from y 611 up to y 243). Right of x 1300 the view opens over the valley: the ridge across it at about y 590 with one turbine at x 1814 (hub y 536, blade tip up to y 501), and below the ridge line the valley floor's hedged fields, far below the camera, down to where the near edge of the felled slope cuts them off; above the ridge, open sky. Focal point: the line where the dark standing forest meets the bright replanted slope. Free zones for the cast, both heads in open sky above the valley: (1) A on the loading bay right of centre, seen full length (head top x 1422, y 469; feet x 1422, y 966), about 120 px right of the end of the far spruce edge; (2) B beside A, further right (head top x 1699, y 479; feet x 1699, y 909), about 80 px clear of the turbine.
scenes.light: Main set: an early-June afternoon, the sun about 50 degrees high in the south-west, behind the camera and to its left. The spruce wall on the left faces east, away from the sun: its face is deep blue-green shade, and its shadow falls across the left half of the road and the timber stack, a soft-edged band ending about the road's centre line. The felled slope is in full sun: the stumps' pale cut tops and the dry brash bright, the young trees fresh green. The far spruce edge is lit on its sunward face. The valley below is hazy and pale, the ridge and turbine paler still. Clear sky with a few small clouds.
scenes.far: The sky, the valley, the ridge and the turbine, the far spruce edge and the gap where the road enters it, the felled and replanted slope with its stumps, brash, young trees and birches, the standing spruce wall on the left, the timber stack, and the road and loading bay drawn complete under where the cast stands.

identity.place: One fictional river valley in a cool, rainy temperate region in early June. A broad valley floor of mixed farms and hedged fields; a mid-sized river winding through it past a riverside food factory and on toward a small market town; on flat fields of the valley floor a 40-hectare solar farm grazed by sheep; on the ridge that closes the valley to the north, about 60 m above its floor, a wind farm of a few large turbines; on the higher hills to the west a working forest of spruce plantations, with native oak and birch woodland along the streams. Every set is a spot in this one valley, so the same turbine ridge, the same river and the same hedged fields recur. No real place is drawn.
architecture: the fields: medium-sized fields of grass and cereal crops bounded by thick hawthorn hedgerows about 2 to 3 m tall, with tall oak trees standing out of the hedges every 60 to 150 m; galvanised steel five-bar field gates 3.6 m wide on timber posts; grass margins between hedge and crop

the farm: a two-storey farmhouse of grey stone with a slate roof and white sash windows; a steel portal-frame barn about 30 m long with grey-green profiled cladding, an open front and a low-pitched roof; a smaller older stone barn; a concrete yard

the river: about 25 m wide, brown-green and clear in the shallows, with gravel bars on the inside of bends, alder and willow along the banks, a grassy flood embankment about 2.5 m high set back from the bank, a steel staff gauge board at a gauging point

the factory: a riverside food factory upstream (a dairy): long low steel-clad sheds in pale grey, four tall stainless steel silos, a loading yard, a concrete outfall headwall in the bank with a pipe discharging into the river; no names or logos

the solar farm: long rows of fixed dark-blue panels on galvanised steel frames facing south, about 0.8 m high at the front edge and 2.75 m at the back, rows about 9 m apart with grass between, a 2 m deer fence on timber posts around it, small green inverter cabins, sheep grazing

the wind farm: a few large three-bladed turbines on the ridge, white-grey towers about 100 m to the hub with rotors about 130 m across, spaced about 650 m apart along the crest, with gravel access tracks

the forest: plantations of dark blue-green Sitka spruce in even blocks about 25 to 30 m tall, felled and replanted in turn, crossed by gravel forest roads; native oak, birch and rowan along the streams; timber stacked at the roadsides
identity.materials: green grass and cereal crops, dark hawthorn hedges, oak and spruce, grey stone and slate, grey-green steel cladding, galvanised steel, stainless steel, white-grey turbine towers, dark-blue solar glass with silver frames, brown-green river water and pale gravel, gravel tracks, wet earth. Palette families in this outdoor world (the set palette was named for rooms): the sky is sky; water and solar glass are glass; distant hills, stone and buildings far away are exterior; grass, crops, hedges and trees are plant; tracks, soil, gravel and the ground are floor; stone walls and concrete are wall; steel cladding and painted metal are wall2; timber (gates, posts, stacked logs) is wood; galvanised and stainless steel are metal; white turbine towers are paper; the few red, orange or yellow things (a tractor, a life ring, a safety sign's border) are accent
inhabited: farming going on: tyre ruts and tramlines in the crops, round bales wrapped in black plastic, a water trough, a gate tied with orange baler twine, a muddy patch at the gateway
the energy and industry around it: the turbine ridge always on the skyline, a wooden-pole power line along a lane, the factory's silos glinting in the distance
care and wear: a mended hedge gap with new posts and wire, a fallen branch, a puddle in a pothole, moss on a stone wall

safety and monitoring things where they really are: a life ring on a post at the river bank, a staff gauge board in the water, a forestry warning sign with a pictogram only, a deer fence around the solar farm
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; a field gate is 3.6 m wide and about 1.1 m tall; a hedgerow is 2 to 3 m tall and about 2 m thick
a hedgerow oak is about 18 to 22 m tall; a mature spruce plantation is about 25 to 30 m tall
a wind turbine is about 100 m to the hub with blades about 65 m long (tip height about 165 m); turbines stand about 650 m apart
a solar panel row is about 4.2 m deep on the ground, 0.8 m high at its front edge and 2.75 m at its back; rows are about 9 m apart
the river is about 25 m wide; the flood embankment about 2.5 m high with a 3 m wide grassy top; a staff gauge board is about 0.1 m wide and up to about 2.6 m long
a forest road has a gravel running width of about 3.4 m; a timber stack is about 3 m tall with logs about 3 to 5 m long
a farm barn's eaves are about 6 m up and its ridge about 9 m
identity.default_light: Early June, a clear afternoon with a few fair-weather cumulus clouds: the sun about 50 degrees high in the south-west, crisp shadows, fresh saturated greens; the distant ridge and hills a little paler and bluer with distance.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one valley (each scene names the ones its camera can see): the white turbines on the northern ridge, a hawthorn hedgerow with a tall oak standing out of it, the river with alder along its banks, dark spruce plantations on the western hills, a galvanised five-bar gate, grazing sheep, the factory's stainless silos in the distance.
avoid: real places, brands, logos, flags, signs with words, names on vehicles
a tropical or desert landscape, palm trees, mountains with snow
a cartoon-perfect countryside: every set shows that land is worked and used
smoke-belching chimneys or a cartoon-evil factory: the factory is an ordinary, tidy plant; any pollution shows only as a real sign (a discoloured plume in the water)
turbines with four blades, lattice towers or blades of uneven length; solar panels facing north
people in the sets (the cast is separate)
objects at the wrong size: a gate reaches a person's waist, a turbine dwarfs everything around it
identity.outside: The valley runs east to west; the turbine ridge closes the view to the north, the forested hills rise to the west, and the market town lies downstream to the east; the sky is big and open.

objects.solar panel row: a long fixed table of solar panels: rectangular dark-blue glass modules (each about 2.3 by 1.1 m, with thin silver aluminium frames and a faint grid of cells) laid two high in portrait, tilted about 25 degrees to face south, the front (lower) edge about 0.8 m above the grass and the back edge about 2.75 m; the table about 4.2 m deep on the ground, carried on galvanised steel posts driven into the ground every few metres with rails under the modules; a cable tray low along the back; rows about 9 m apart with grass between
objects.inverter cabin: a small steel cabin about 6 m long, 2.5 m wide and 2.9 m tall, painted dark green, on a concrete plinth: louvred vents along its sides, two steel doors, a cable duct entering at its base; no words, only a small yellow triangle pictogram for electricity
objects.weather station: a slim galvanised mast about 3 m tall on a small concrete base with a short cross-arm: a small white glass dome sensor (pyranometer) and a white disc-shaped temperature shield on it, a grey box at the mast's foot
objects.wind turbine: a three-bladed horizontal-axis wind turbine: a smooth white-grey tapering tubular steel tower about 100 m tall, a long rounded nacelle on top facing into the wind, three slender tapering blades about 65 m long set 120 degrees apart on a rounded hub; all three blades the same length; a small square door at the tower's foot and a gravel crane pad beside it
objects.sheep: a hill-breed ewe about 0.7 m tall at the shoulder and 1.2 m long: a woolly off-white body, a white or dark face, thin dark legs, short ears; grazing with its head down or lying in shade
objects.meadow: a wildflower meadow left unplanted: tall grasses about 0.5 to 0.8 m high with ox-eye daisies, red clover, knapweed and buttercups, a few flowers above the grass; its edge cut short along the track
objects.gravel track: an unsealed track about 3.5 m wide of compacted grey gravel with two worn wheel lines and a grassy strip down the middle, its edges ragged where grass grows in
objects.distant ridge: a long, smooth ridge about 60 m above the valley floor, its slopes a patchwork of small hedged fields and a few woods, softer and bluer with distance; gravel tracks zig-zag up to the turbines on its crest
objects.wheat crop: a field of winter wheat in early June, about 0.85 m tall: dense upright green stems and leaves with the ears just out, a silvery sheen where the wind bends it; its edge a clean line of stems
objects.tramlines: the paired wheel tracks left unsown through the crop for the sprayer: two parallel bare-earth lines about 0.5 m wide and 1.8 m apart, repeating every 24 m across the field, running straight to the far hedge
objects.hedgerow: a hawthorn hedge about 2.5 m tall and 2 m thick, dense dark green with a few creamy flower clusters left, its base thicker with brambles and nettles and a grass strip in front
objects.oak tree: a mature English oak about 20 m tall standing out of the hedge: a short thick trunk, broad rounded crown of heavy twisting limbs, dense mid-green foliage in clumps with darker hollows
objects.steel barn: a steel portal-frame farm building about 30 m long and 18 m wide: a low-pitched roof of grey-green profiled steel sheet (eaves 6 m, ridge 9 m), grey-green profiled walls on three sides and open along one long side, showing the steel portal frames inside, a concrete apron in front
objects.farmhouse: a two-storey farmhouse of grey rubble stone with a slate roof and a stone chimney at each gable, white-painted sash windows in a regular row, a porch over the front door; no name sign
objects.round bales: cylindrical bales of silage about 1.2 m across and 1.2 m long, wrapped tight in black plastic film, stacked in a pyramid of two layers
objects.soil auger and bucket: a steel soil auger about 1 m long with a T-handle and a half-cylinder blade holding a core of dark earth, lying on the grass beside a plastic bucket of soil samples in small bags
objects.river: a lowland river about 25 m wide: brown-green water, clear in the shallows with gravel showing, darker in mid-channel, a gentle current marked by a few ripples and V-shaped wakes behind stones; earth banks with grass and reeds at the edge
objects.flood embankment: a grassed earth flood bank about 2.5 m tall: smooth sloping sides at about 1 in 3, a flat crest about 3 m wide with a mown path along it, set back from the river with a strip of floodplain grass between
objects.staff gauge: a narrow vertical steel board about 0.1 m wide and 2.6 m long fixed to a steel post driven into the riverbed in the shallows: white enamel with black bar marks every 10 cm and a thicker bar every metre (no numbers drawn), the water line crossing it
objects.life ring post: a red-painted steel post about 1.7 m tall with a lidded red box on top holding an orange life ring with a coiled throw line; no words
objects.outfall headwall: a small concrete wall about 2 m wide set into the river bank, with a round pipe end about 0.4 m across opening just above normal water level, a flap valve over it, a few stones around its foot
objects.alder tree: a common alder 12 to 13 m tall growing at the water's edge: one or two dark grey trunks, a narrow rounded crown of dark green leaves, roots showing in the bank
objects.factory: a tidy food factory (a dairy) seen far away: long low pale-grey steel-clad sheds about 9 m tall with low-pitched roofs, four tall stainless steel silos about 21 m tall standing in a row beside them, a loading yard with a parked tanker; no chimneys, no names
objects.spruce plantation: an even-aged block of Sitka spruce about 27 m tall: tall straight trunks in close rows, narrow pointed crowns of dense dark blue-green needles making a tall dark wall with a ragged top of spires; inside the edge, dim with dead lower branches
objects.forest road: a gravel forest road with a 3.4 m running width, cambered, with a grass verge and a drainage ditch on each side and a wider gravel loading bay where timber is stacked and lorries turn
objects.timber stack: a roadside stack of spruce logs about 4 m long and 0.2 to 0.4 m across, piled about 3 m high and 12 m long on bearers, the pale cut ends facing the road with their rings showing
objects.felled and replanted slope: a hillside felled about two years ago: low stumps with pale cut tops, cut branches (brash) raked into lines along the contour, young spruce about 0.5 m tall planted in rows between the brash lines, a few young broadleaves in pale tree shelters about 1.2 m tall, foxgloves and willowherb flowering
objects.birch tree: a silver birch about 14 m tall with a slender white trunk marked by dark diamonds, a light airy crown of small bright green leaves
objects.forestry safety sign: a small square sign on a timber post at the roadside, about 0.6 m across, with a black pictogram of a falling tree and a person inside a red-bordered triangle on white; no words
objects.valley view: the open valley seen from the hills: hedged fields of greens and yellows, a river winding through with alders along it, a few farms, the far ridge with turbines, all paler and bluer with distance
